<!-- isms:begin id=overview.intro -->

## Document Overview {#sec-overview}

This Access Control Policy establishes the requirements to ensure the protection of
{{< var environment_name >}}s within the scope of {{< var organisation >}}'s {{< var isms_name >}}
by managing access rights. This policy supports compliance with relevant standards (e.g. ISO/IEC
27001), ensuring that access to information is based on business needs and aligned with security
requirements.

This document covers:

<!-- isms:end id=overview.intro -->

<!-- isms:begin id=overview.contents -->

- [Access Control Principles](#sec-principles)
- [User Access Management](#sec-user-access)
- [Authentication Principles](#sec-authentication)
- [Privileged Access Management](#sec-privileged-access)
- [Physical Access](#sec-physical-access)
- [Network Access](#sec-network-access)
- [Operating System Access](#sec-os-access)
- [Information System Access](#sec-information-system-access)
- [Monitoring and Logging](#sec-monitoring)

<!-- isms:end id=overview.contents -->

<!-- isms:end id=overview -->

<!-- isms:begin id=scope hint="Name the environments, applications and services in scope, and the categories of person to whom this policy applies." -->

## Document Scope {#sec-scope}

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary staff, service accounts,
and any other individuals with access to {{< var environment_name >}}s. The scope of this policy
includes the infrastructure, applications and services that support each
{{< var environment_name >}}, referred to in this document as "information systems".

<!-- isms:end id=scope -->

<!-- isms:begin id=conventions -->

## Conventions used in this Document {#sec-conventions}

| Term   | Definition                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| Shall  | A mandatory requirement of this policy   |
| Should | A recommended requirement of this policy |
| May    | An optional requirement of this policy   |

<!-- isms:end id=conventions -->

<!-- isms:begin id=principles -->

## Access Control Principles {#sec-principles}

Access to information systems shall be managed according to the following principles:

- **Need to Know:** Access shall be granted based on the specific tasks a user must perform or a
  system account is designated for.
- **Least Privilege:** Accounts shall be granted the minimum permissions necessary to perform their
  roles.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):** Access rights shall be assigned according to defined roles
  within the organisation.
- **Segregation of Duties:** No individual shall have control over all aspects of any critical
  system or process.

<!-- isms:end id=principles -->

<!-- isms:begin id=user-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=user-access.intro -->

## User Access Management {#sec-user-access}

All user access shall be managed by an appropriate role as described in the {{< var organisation >}}
roles and responsibilities framework.

- **User registration, de-registration, and access authorisation:** Formal procedures for adding,
  changing, or removing user access shall be implemented.

<!-- isms:end id=user-access.intro -->

<!-- isms:begin id=user-access.approval-chain hint="Which roles approve new or changed access at your institution?" -->

- New users or changes to user access shall be approved by:
  - The {{< var roles.asset_owner >}} (for a project or study)
  - The {{< var roles.environment_owner >}} (for infrastructure and code management)
  - The {{< var roles.service_owner >}} or their delegate (for IT service access)

<!-- isms:end id=user-access.approval-chain -->

- **Removal of access rights:** Access shall be removed promptly upon termination or role change.

<!-- isms:begin id=user-access.review-cadence hint="How often are access rights reviewed?" -->

- **Review of access rights:** Reviews of user access rights shall be conducted at least every
  {{< var review.access_review_period >}} to ensure appropriateness.

<!-- isms:end id=user-access.review-cadence -->

<!-- isms:end id=user-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=authentication -->

## Authentication Principles {#sec-authentication}

All users and systems shall comply with {{< var organisation >}}'s authentication standards and
policies, including multi-factor authentication where required.

<!-- isms:end id=authentication -->

<!-- isms:begin id=privileged-access -->

## Privileged Access Management {#sec-privileged-access}

Administrative or privileged accounts shall be tightly controlled and limited to authorised
personnel. Privileged accounts should be used only for administrative purposes. Privileged access
management shall follow a formal process that grants only the minimum privileges necessary to
perform the assigned role or task. A formal record of all allocated privileges shall be maintained.

<!-- isms:end id=privileged-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=physical-access -->

## Physical Access {#sec-physical-access}

Physical access shall be granted only upon the authority of the facility owner or service manager.
All physical information systems shall be protected in accordance with their value and
classification per {{< var organisation >}}'s information management policies. Approved personnel
shall be responsible for physical security measures to prevent unauthorised access to devices or
data.

<!-- isms:end id=physical-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=network-access -->

## Network Access {#sec-network-access}

- Diagnostic and configuration ports shall be enabled only for approved business reasons.
- All unused ports shall be disabled or removed.
- Changes to network configuration affecting {{< var environment_abbr >}} networks shall be risk
  assessed and recorded.
- Network segregation shall be implemented according to risk assessments to protect sensitive
  information.

<!-- isms:end id=network-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=os-access -->

## Operating System Access {#sec-os-access}

- Users shall authenticate as authorised users at log-on.
- Passwords shall be managed in accordance with {{< var organisation >}} password policies.
- Sessions shall automatically lock after periods of inactivity.
- Default operating system accounts shall be disabled, deleted, or have default passwords changed
  upon system deployment.

<!-- isms:end id=os-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=information-system-access -->

## Information System Access {#sec-information-system-access}

- Accounts without adequate assurance shall be disabled until appropriate verification is provided.
- Removal of accounts shall include removal of associated access rights.
- {{< var roles.environment_owner >}}s shall implement appropriate segregation of information assets
  on networks, grouping information assets as appropriate to achieve the required network
  segregation.

<!-- isms:end id=information-system-access -->

<!-- isms:begin id=monitoring -->

## Monitoring and Logging {#sec-monitoring}

Access to {{< var environment_name >}}s shall be logged and monitored for security incident
investigation purposes. Logs should include a timestamp, the user's identity, and the reason for
access. Periodic reviews shall detect unauthorised access attempts. Any anomalies or violations
shall be assessed and reported as information security incidents in accordance with
{{< var organisation >}} incident management procedures.

<!-- isms:end id=monitoring -->
